blocks.text: Langley Foreclosures and Court-Ordered Sales: streets and boundaries

items.t: The Township of Langley states it is required by the Local Government Act to sell at its annual tax sale every property whose taxes have not been paid for three years.
The Province's courthouse list names the New Westminster Law Courts, Begbie Square, 651 Carnarvon Street, New Westminster, as a Supreme Court location serving the region.

blocks.text: Langley Foreclosures and Court-Ordered Sales: the housing stock

items.t: Township tax-sale lists show the range directly: the Township's 2026 public notice lists properties by street address, parcel identifier (PID) and legal description across rural and urban Township lots, including strata-plan lots.

blocks.text: Langley Foreclosures and Court-Ordered Sales: rules that affect buyers

items.t: A BC foreclosure must be started by petition under Supreme Court Civil Rule 21-7, with every person whose interest is to be extinguished made a respondent; the Langley-specific work is in the municipal tax-sale rules below, not in a different court process.
The Township sells tax-sale properties "as is" without warranty or guarantee, and states it makes no representation about the condition or quality of a property sold.
The Township's upset price — the floor bid — equals all outstanding taxes, penalties, interest, 5% tax sale costs, and Land Title Office fees.
A petitioner who registers a certificate of pending litigation (CPL) against a Langley title binds anyone who later registers an interest in that property.

blocks.text: Langley Foreclosures and Court-Ordered Sales: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The Township must advertise its tax sale in a local paper not less than 3 and not more than 10 days before the sale, so the confirmed property list appears only shortly before auction day.
A purchase at a BC municipal tax sale is subject to property transfer tax on the fair market value of the property — the Township states this in its own tax-sale material.

Both the City of Langley and the Township of Langley are designated taxable areas for the provincial Speculation and Vacancy Tax, so an empty court-bought home in either municipality still needs the annual declaration.

blocks.text: Langley Foreclosures and Court-Ordered Sales: development and new projects

items.t: No single development project changes the foreclosure picture in Langley; what changes the stock is the two municipalities' approvals pipelines, and the Township's own tax-sale notice shows the pipeline's other end — newly built strata lots (legal descriptions in the 2026 notice include strata plans EPS8852 and EPS9310) already appearing on a delinquent-tax list. STATUS: Township 2026 tax sale notice read 2026-11-03.

blocks.text: Langley Foreclosures and Court-Ordered Sales: costs and taxes

items.t: The Township's tax-sale costs are built into its upset price: outstanding taxes, penalties, interest, 5% tax sale costs and Land Title Office fees.
Costs in an uncontested Rule 21-7 foreclosure are assessed under Scale A, the lowest scale in the rules' costs appendix.

blocks.text: Langley Foreclosures and Court-Ordered Sales: getting around

items.t: The Township's tax sale is held at the Township of Langley Civic Facility, 20338 – 65 Avenue, Langley — the same building bidders pre-register at on sale morning.

blocks.text: Langley Foreclosures and Court-Ordered Sales: risks and due diligence

items.t: Confirm the municipality first: a legal description in the Township's notice is stated in New Westminster District terms (for example "LT 1 SEC 2 TWP 7 NWD"), and searching the wrong municipality's tax-sale list is the most basic Langley error.
Township tax-sale properties are sold "as is" with no representation about condition or quality — inspection and title diligence happen before the auction, not after.

faq.q: If a property is in "Langley," which tax sale do I watch?
faq.a: The one run by the municipality the property actually sits in. The City of Langley and the Township of Langley are separate municipalities with separate tax rolls; the Township holds its auction at its Civic Facility, 20338 – 65 Avenue, and a City property never appears on the Township's list, or the reverse. Check the municipal address, not the mailing city name.

faq.q: When is the Township of Langley tax sale and how do I bid?
faq.a: The Township holds it as a public auction on the last Monday in September at 10 a.m. — September 28 in 2026 — in Council Chambers at the Civic Facility, 20338 – 65 Avenue. Bidders pre-register that morning, between 9:15 and 9:50 a.m. for the 2026 sale, and bidding is accepted on all listed properties.

faq.q: Can the owner get a Township tax-sale property back?
faq.a: Yes — the owner has one year after the sale to redeem it. During that year the purchaser holds a sale that the owner can unwind by paying what the Local Government Act requires, which is why a tax-sale purchase is not the same as a completed court-ordered sale with court-approved title.

faq.q: What if my delinquent taxes are in the Township — is there a deadline before the auction?
faq.a: Yes. The Township states delinquent taxes must be paid by August 31 of the calendar year to keep the property out of that year's tax sale process, ahead of the late-September auction date.

faq.q: What does "subject to court approval" mean for my offer?
faq.a: Where the court has directed sale by contract conditional on the approval of the court (Rule 13-5 (4) (b)), the person with conduct of sale applies under Rule 21-7 (9) for an order confirming the sale, directing the proceeds and vesting title in the purchaser — until that order, the sale is not final.

faq.q: Can someone outbid my accepted offer?
faq.a: The court's sale directions may define the rights of a person to bid, make offers or meet bids (Rule 13-5 (4) (d)), and the Supreme Court's practice direction PD-66 governs foreclosure proceedings — so a competing bid at the approval stage is a real possibility in this process.
